newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan opposition name new administration lineup.
newsitem.headline: Afghan opposition name new administration lineup.

text.p: The Afghan opposition alliance named a new prime minister and defence minister in a shake-up of its administration announced on Wednesday.

An opposition spokesman, speaking on Radio Mashhad, broadcasting from Iran, said that Burhanuddin Rabbani, head of the administration ousted from Kabul by the Taleban Islamic militia last September, would remain as president, but that Abdur Rahim Gaffurzai would become prime minister.
Gaffurzai, foreign minister in the ousted administration, formerly served in Afghanistan's mission to the United Nations and has been the opposition's main spokesman abroad.

Ahmed Shah Masood, the ousted administration's top military commander, returns to the post of defence minister. Masood is currently directing the battle against the Taleban on the front line north of Kabul.
Abdul Malik, the general who joined the Taleban in May only to turn against them shortly afterwards, has become foreign minister.

Vice-presidential posts went to various parties which have pledged their loyalty to the opposition alliance. Of three vice-presidential posts created, one went to the mainly Shi'ite Moslem Hezb-e-Wahadat party, one to Harakat-e- Islami, and the third was left vacant.
The new line up was announced after a three-day meeting between senior members of the tripartite anti-Taleban alliance in the Salang Pass 75 miles (120 km) north of Kabul.
Analysts in Kabul said that the new administration was an attempt to present a credible alternative to the Taleban.
"They need to present a united front against the Taleban, and show the world that they can provide an alternative." said the analyst late on Wednesday.
Opposition forces have been poised less than 12 miles (20 km) from Kabul for more than three weeks. Despite daily skirmishes and artillery duels there has been little movement in the front line.
If the meeting has resolved the differences between the alliance's factions, they would be in a stronger position to launch a combined offensive on the capital.
